In a high school, a group of students was asked about whether they prefer apples, oranges, or bananas. The results are given in the two-way frequency table below.

|  | Apple | Orange | Banana | Totals |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Girls | $11$ | $8$ | $7$ | $26$ |
| Boys | $12$ | $6$ | $6$ | $24$ |
| Totals | $23$ | $14$ | $13$ | $50$ |

Estimate the probability that a randomly chosen student in the group preferred apples or bananas or is a girl.

> A calculator is required to answer this question.

Susan conducted a survey of some children in a park. She asked them if they like the colors blue and yellow. Her findings are summarized in the two-way frequency table below.

|  | Likes blue | Doesn't like blue | Totals |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Likes yellow | $12$ | $3$ | $15$ |
| Doesn't like yellow | $8$ | $2$ | $10$ |
| Totals | $20$ | $5$ | $25$ |

Estimate the probability that a randomly chosen child likes blue or yellow but not both colors.

> A calculator is required to answer this question.

Martin surveyed some students in a school, asking them if they have cats or dogs at home. His findings are summarized in the two-way frequency table below.

|  | Has a dog | Doesn't have a dog | Totals |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Has a cat | $6$ | $9$ | $15$ |
| Doesn't have a cat | $10$ | $7$ | $17$ |
| Totals | $16$ | $16$ | $32$ |

Estimate the probability that a randomly chosen student in the school has either a cat or a dog but not both.

The employees and the interns of a company were asked whether they commute to work by car or by bus. The results of the survey are summarized in the two-way frequency table below.

|  | Employee | Intern | Totals |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Car | $24$ | $16$ | $40$ |
| Bus | $26$ | $14$ | $40$ |
| Totals | $50$ | $30$ | $80$ |

Let $I$ be the event that a randomly selected person is a **"Intern"**, and $B$ be the event that a randomly selected person commutes to work by **"Bus"**. Estimate $P(I\cup B).$
